description: The decision game's words: stages of situations (points), each with the choices a learner can make. One point is one reported decision; its id is a data-question-id row on the page, and its outcome codes are that row's data-measures, never in here. Ask the person for every rule and source you were not given.

title.description: The game's title, on its first screen and its debrief.

stages.description: The game in order: a stage is a place or a moment, holding one or more points.

scene.description: Where and when the stage happens, one short line above each of its situations.

points.description: The decisions of this stage, in order.

id.description: The interaction id the LMS receives: ASCII, unique in the lecture, and the data-question-id of one row on the page. Take it from the client's alignment document; never invent it.

situation.description: What the learner faces, before any choice: the behaviour the outcome is about, in a situation they would meet.

choices.description: What the learner can do here, at least two. The first correct one is what the platform plays as right, the first wrong one as wrong.

id.description: The response the LMS receives: ASCII (a, b, c, or a short word), unique within the point. Not none, which means no decision was made.

label.description: The behaviour, as the learner would do it, in their words. The feedback repeats it, so it names an act, not a verdict.

result.description: How this choice is reported: correct and wrong are scored, neutral (a hesitant or partly right act) is recorded and not scored.

severity.description: How much is at stake in this choice; it travels with the answer. Optional.

consequence.description: What happened because of the choice, shown BEFORE the rule. A consequence, not a judgement.

rule.description: The rule the situation tests, shown after the consequence and in the debrief.

source.description: The citation the learner reads under the rule («المصدر: …»). Ask the person; never invent it. Left empty, the release lists it as left for the person.

commitment.description: Optional: a closing question the learner answers in their own words, after the debrief. Their sentence is reported as a fill-in with id commitment.

prompt.description: The question, about what they will do next time.
